title: PowerDisplay doesn't find my monitor (KVM switch)

status.label: Verify unavailable monitor-control status
status.detail: The reporter now suspects the KVM does not forward DDC/CI. Windows can still display through the switch.

next_action.label: Compare direct and KVM control discovery.
next_action.reason: Check whether PowerDisplay distinguishes a Windows-visible display from a usable hardware-control path.

judgment.rationale: Distinguish a Windows-enumerated monitor from one whose DDC/CI handle is unavailable; do not promise control if the KVM blocks that channel.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the discovery-status proposal with a direct-versus-KVM comparison.

fix_assessment.rationale: Discovery uses DDC/CI physical handles and stable DevicePath. The reporter now suspects missing DDC/CI forwarding; this proposal addresses the status shown to users, not hardware control through an incompatible switch.

proposed_fixes.title: Explain when a Windows-visible monitor has no usable DDC/CI path
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The KVM may leave the display visible to Windows while preventing PowerDisplay from obtaining a usable physical-monitor handle; this is a hypothesis.
plan: Reproduce with the display directly connected and through the KVM.
Trace Windows enumeration separately from physical-handle and DevicePath availability.
If currently conflated, show a specific unavailable-control reason without claiming that the monitor can be controlled.
verification: Verify direct-connect and KVM cases report distinct discovery/control states.
Verify DDC/CI-capable displays retain their controls.

confidence.rationale: The DDC path and KVM relationship are source-grounded, but the KVM’s behavior is unconfirmed.

issue_context.summary: PowerDisplay does not find the reporter’s monitor through a KVM switch.
known_information: The report explicitly identifies a KVM switch and says the monitor is not found by PowerDisplay.
Current DDC discovery needs a usable physical-monitor handle and stable Windows DevicePath; a KVM may pass display output but block DDC/CI.
inferences: The reporter now suspects their KVM does not support DDC/CI. The thread does not explicitly record a successful direct-connect control test.
issue_context.analysis: Distinguish a Windows-enumerated monitor from one whose DDC/CI handle is unavailable; do not promise control if the KVM blocks that channel.
information_gaps: Maintainer comparison of direct and KVM control availability, and whether current PowerDisplay explains the difference.

actions.label: Compare direct and KVM monitor control

reproduce.title: Distinguish display enumeration from DDC/CI availability
prerequisites: An external DDC/CI monitor and a KVM that may not forward DDC/CI.
setup: Enable DDC/CI on the display and use the same monitor and connection type in both tests.
steps: Connect the monitor directly and record Windows enumeration and PowerDisplay hardware controls.
Repeat through the KVM, comparing physical-handle discovery and the status shown in PowerDisplay.
reproduce.expected_result: Display output and hardware control are reported separately; PowerDisplay does not imply DDC/CI is available when the switch blocks it.
